title: [Decision] Push delivery data: name the server that sent a push, so a mobile shell with several saved servers opens a tap on the right one
body:
repo:mobile#1 · os-justin · session_01QSeKYnW1Xf6HDSWz1eGAqv

Ruled: 6593872191 · letter B · 2026-11-03T02:26Z

Filing category ②: a decision only the maintainer can make (the shape of a public contract). It came from objectstack-ai/mobile#174, where the dev stopped on that card's own stop condition.

## 维护者速读

- **一句话问题：** App 里存了多台服务器后，点开 B 服务器发来的推送，会在当前的 A 服务器上打开；推送内容里没有任何「是哪台服务器发的」信息，App 无从判断。
- **为什么现在定：** 推送契约还在 objectstack-ai/objectstack#29218（草稿，未合并）里，现在加一个可选字段最便宜；合并后再加就是第二次放宽契约。
- **推荐：** B。Console 注册设备时报上自己加载的来源（就是 App 存下的那个地址），服务器存进设备记录，发推送时原样带回。
- **需要你做的：** 选 A / B / C。

## Governing text

- `packages/spec/src/api/push-delivery.zod.ts` at objectstack-ai/objectstack#29218 head `aff751de`, lines 90-99. `PushDeliveryDataSchema` is a `z.object` with exactly `notificationId` (required) and `route` (optional, same-server relative path). It has no host, origin or server key.
- The file is absent on `main` (re-check: `git cat-file -e origin/main:packages/spec/src/api/push-delivery.zod.ts`, which fails).
- ADR-0012 (push renderer output: title, body, data, sound, badge) carries no identity either.
- APNs and FCM tell the app nothing about the sender. Every saved server registers the same device token, so the shell cannot tell senders apart locally.

## Options

| Option | What | Customer-visible effect | Effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | The push channel adds a server-origin key to `PushDeliveryDataSchema`, taken from the server's configured public URL. | Taps open on the right server, except where the server is reached under another hostname or behind a rewriting proxy. There the origin does not match a saved host, so the tap is dropped. That failure is safe but silent. | One optional key in #29218, plus one line in the #29041 channel. No precedent. |
| B | The Console sends the origin it was loaded from (`window.location.origin`, which is exactly the host the shell saved) in `RegisterDeviceRequest`. The server stores it on the `UserDevice` row, and the push channel copies it into the push data. | Taps open on the right server in every deployment shape, because the value is the host the shell itself saved. | One optional member each on `RegisterDeviceRequestSchema`, `UserDeviceSchema` and `PushDeliveryDataSchema`, all inside #29218 before it merges, plus the Console's registration call. No precedent. |
| C | No platform change. The shell keeps routing on the current connection and documents the limit. | Wrong-server taps stay. | None. |

## Four axes

- **Long-term soundness (weight first):** B ties the identity to the exact registration that receives the push, which is how multi-account mobile clients usually scope their tokens. A depends on the server knowing its own public URL, which proxies break.
- **Real business pull:** saved connections shipped in objectstack-ai/mobile#173, so the defect is reachable today for any user with two servers. No store users yet.
- **AI-error prevention:** with B, a mismatch is structurally impossible because the value round-trips. With A, a misconfigured public URL fails silently. With C, the wrong page opens with no signal.
- **Startup focus:** B adds three optional members, all in a PR that has not merged, so there is no second widening later. C adds nothing but keeps the defect.

```
os-decision-facets
① long-term: B round-trips the registered origin; A depends on server self-knowledge
② pull: reachable since mobile#173 for any multi-server user
③ AI-error: B structurally matched; A silent drop on proxy; C wrong page
④ scope: B three optional members inside an unmerged PR; C none
Prior rulings read: push payload server origin|PushDeliveryDataSchema → 2 queries, 0 rulings; ADR-0012 none on identity; thread: none
```

**Recommendation: B.**
- Confidence gap: not yet checked whether the Console's registration call (objectstack-ai/objectstack#29042) can send the loaded origin before #29218 merges.
- Self-check: on axis ① alone, B wins; ②③④ do not flip it.

**After the ruling:**
- The spec seat adds the member(s) to #29218, or to a follow-up PR if #29218 has merged.
- objectstack-ai/mobile#174 resumes with a host lookup through the saved-connections `switch` path.

Clause-②: yes (this widens a published-to-be contract), so the spec lane owns the change.
